clue.text: Word, possibly Excel or PowerPoint, for certain applications

definitions.text: Word, possibly Excel or PowerPoint, for certain applications

parts.words: Word, possibly Excel or PowerPoint, for certain applications
parts.note: Word, Excel and PowerPoint look like the Microsoft programs, but here they are simply examples of words of more than one syllable

explanation.surface: A list of Microsoft Office programs used for particular software jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised Word, Excel and PowerPoint read as office software; the clue really says that the word 'Excel' or 'PowerPoint' is an example of a long, many-syllabled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Excel has two syllables and PowerPoint three, so each is a word of several syllables.

clue.text: Carrying a gun past supremo seen around clubs

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces is seen around another, so it wraps the single letter for clubs

parts.note: pa. is the dictionary abbreviation for past, as in pa.t. for past tense
a king is a supreme ruler
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: An armed figure walks past a boss surrounded by nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang usage: someone packing is carrying a concealed firearm.

clue.text: Couples may be found here

parts.note: suggests a place where pairs of lovers meet, but golfers play in couples (pairs) on a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A spot where romantic pairs tend to gather.
explanation.walkthrough: Couples are pairs of golfers playing together; the word for a seaside golf course also means the rings that couple together in a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal golf course is called by this name, and golfers play there in pairs.

clue.text: Hold worker day after day before in bank

indicators.note: the day pieces sit in the word for bank

parts.note: a store is a bank or reserve of supplies

indicators.note: one day comes after the other, so the single letter follows the eve

parts.note: the eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: An employee clocking in day after day at a bank's strongroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A docker who loads and unloads the hold of a ship is a hold worker.

clue.text: Misses that is, missing blokes

indicators.note: the letters for 'that is' go missing from the word for misses

parts.note: misses are young women, ladies
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A wistful remark that some women are missing the men in their lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Lads and blokes are both informal words for men or young men.

clue.text: End scoffed about supporter accepting own goal

indicators.note: the word for scoffed goes about the rest

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed means ate

indicators.note: the supporter accepts the own-goal letters inside it

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A sports report: the game ended with jeering about a fan who put through his own net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' is a verb here, to abolish, not the close of a match; 'accepting' builds the inner BROGA before 'about' wraps the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or agreement is to repeal it, bringing it to an end.

clue.text: Record covering unknown composer

indicators.note: the record covers, wraps round, the unknown letter

parts.note: a list is a written record
Z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: An album sleeve covering a recording by an anonymous composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Big head possesses synapse's top speed

indicators.note: the word for big holds a letter within it

parts.note: fat means big, bulky

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: A big-headed neuroscientist boasting about the top speed of nerve signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big head' reads as a boaster, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastness can mean swiftness, the quality of being fast, though it more often means a stronghold.

clue.text: Bird's well up over quarry

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits over the second
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: so is an interjection like well, opening a sentence
prey is quarry, a hunted animal

explanation.surface: A bird soaring high over its quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey.

clue.text: One striving in opposition keeping goal, repelling United

indicators.note: the shortened word keeps the goal inside it
repelling means driving out, so the letter for United goes

parts.note: counter means against, in opposition
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A footballer on the opposing side keeps goal and fends off United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelling' removes United, leaving CONTER, which 'keeping' then opens; the football surface hides that goal simply means aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone competing for a prize, a person who strives to win.

clue.text: Ship carrying around dead fish

indicators.note: the ship carries the other letters inside it

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
ca. is short for circa, around
D is the abbreviation for dead, as on family trees

explanation.surface: A vessel bringing in a catch of dead fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a fish, the horse mackerel; this is its plural.

clue.text: Heads of illegal syndicate prosecuted and released

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters

parts.note: sued means took legal action against

explanation.surface: The leaders of a criminal gang were tried and then let go.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement or publication that is issued has been put out, released to the public.

clue.text: Revolutionary adopting incoherent argument with other ends

indicators.note: the ends of each of these four words are their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A radical takes up a muddled line of argument with a different conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with other ends' seems to describe a changed argument, but 'ends' picks the outer letters of adopting, incoherent, argument and other.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolutionary stirs up political unrest, which is what an agitator does.

clue.text: Ape with aristocrat, famous in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: a nob is a toff or aristocrat
big means famous, as in big name

explanation.surface: A monkey and a famous nobleman beating a hasty retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: The gibbon is a small tree-dwelling ape of south-east Asia.

clue.text: Joyful whip provided by sick heart

parts.note: to whip is to beat
if means provided that

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A cheerful flogging delivered by someone with a weak heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A beatific expression is blissful and serene, radiating happiness.

clue.text: Turn craft over in empty sky for manoeuvres

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular answer: a strategy is a plan of manoeuvres

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go in the emptied sky
emptying a word leaves only its outer letters
turning something over reverses it, so these words read backwards

parts.note: to turn (sour, say) is to get (sour), become
art means craft, skill

explanation.surface: A pilot turns an aircraft upside down in a clear sky during aerobatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn craft over' reads as flying a loop, but 'over' reverses the two pieces to give TRATEG; 'empty' and 'in' handle the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategy is the planning of military moves, the art of manoeuvring forces.

clue.text: Subsidence in a cellar? Time for spades

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, Time standing for spades

parts.note: a basement is a cellar
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A builder finds sinking in the basement and says it is time for shovels.
explanation.definitionFit: Abatement is a lessening or dying down, and subsidence also means the easing of something.

clue.text: Wood board with overlapping edges for home

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber

indicators.note: the two pieces overlap where their edges meet, so the shared letter appears once

parts.note: to board is to lodge, reside

explanation.surface: Carpentry: wooden boards fitted with overlapping edges, as in clapboard siding for a house.
explanation.walkthrough: FIR ends with R and RESIDE begins with it; 'with overlapping edges' merges that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for home and family life, the hearth at its centre.

clue.text: Claimed a career holds back scholarly life

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse
the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that a career is on hold while they return to university.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and learning, the scholarly life.

clue.text: Seaman beginning to sail globe in hold

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a rating

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: A sailor setting out to sail round the world in a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to take in and retain, to hold within.

clue.text: Caught in Amsterdam selecting girl

indicators.note: the letters are caught inside the two words

explanation.surface: A young woman picked out on the streets of Amsterdam.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old or poetic word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Once irregularly covered by dead small spots

indicators.note: the picked letters are covered by the word for dead, sitting inside it

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king

indicators.note: taking every other letter, here the first and third

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Dead, small spots occasionally covered over, like faded blemishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' looks like a noun echoing the surface, but it is the verb finds; 'irregularly' and 'covered by' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to find it, and locates means finds the position of.

clue.text: Sparkling drink unit's drunk before daybreak …

indicators.note: the drink piece comes before the letter for daybreak
the drink has drunk, taken in, the unit

parts.note: Sprite is a brand of fizzy lemonade
I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit
the break, or start, of day is its first letter

explanation.surface: A unit of booze downed before dawn, leading into the next clue's fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' puts I inside SPRITE; the ellipsis links the surface to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means lively and full of energy, a sense shared by sparkling conversation.

clue.text: Fire one losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: An order to sack one employee, who ends up decapitated.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a domestic fire on a hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: … effervescence precedes spasm of the digestive system

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: pep is liveliness, effervescence
a tic is a twitch or spasm

explanation.surface: Fizz from the previous clue's drink brings on a spasm in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Peptic relates to digestion, as in a peptic ulcer of the stomach.

clue.text: Tantalise, then answer oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Tease someone, then give your answer in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment with something just out of reach, a way to taunt.

clue.text: Very big match changing halves

indicators.note: the two halves of the word swap places, as teams change ends at half time

parts.note: a game is a match

explanation.surface: An enormous football match where the teams change ends at half time.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for huge, enormous.

clue.text: Feeling sorry for one called 'round'

indicators.note: the word for called goes round the numeral

parts.note: rung means telephoned, called
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone regretting having been summoned for a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the thing called, but it tells RUNG to go round I.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, so this means regretting or repenting.

clue.text: Smart European inclined to accept Government being gauche

parts.note: in means fashionable, smart

indicators.note: the word for inclined accepts the government letter inside it

parts.note: leant means inclined, tilted

explanation.surface: A stylish European politician tilting towards government looks awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward and graceless, lacking polish.

clue.text: One gives complaint purchasing new player

indicators.note: purchasing means taking on, so the complaint takes in the new letter

parts.note: a beef is a grumble, a complaint
an actress is a stage player

explanation.surface: A grumble about a company buying a new star performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactress is a woman who donates money or help, one who gives.
